title: Ruanda-Urundi
capsule: Ruanda-Urundi was a League of Nations Class B mandate and later UN Trust Territory administered by Belgium from 1922 to 1962, comprising the former German East African kingdoms of Rwanda and Burundi, seized by Belgian forces during the East African campaign of 1916. Belgium governed through indirect rule that reinforced and systematized Tutsi–Hutu social distinctions — introducing racial identity cards in 1933 — deepening ethnic hierarchies that would have catastrophic long-term consequences. Driven by African nationalist pressure and the destabilizing example of Congolese independence in 1960, the territory split into the independent Republic of Rwanda and Kingdom of Burundi on 1 July 1962, following intercommunal violence in Rwanda in 1959–1961 that had already overthrown the Tutsi monarchy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territory's boundaries are very precisely established from Belgian colonial administrative records and League of Nations mandate documentation, inherited from the German colonial era and formally demarcated in treaties.
